transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... recently I was working on my aunt’s memorial piece, and I just kept getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow. It felt like... like one wrong photo placement or a bad color choice would mean I didn’t love her enough. I'm used to second-guessing my art, but I couldn’t just brush these thoughts off like my normal creative doubts. It was really bothering me, so I figured I should talk to someone.
When those thoughts came up, did you feel driven to do certain things repeatedly or follow specific steps to make the anxiety go away?

Yeah, I do. I'll end up... rereading the label text, or just nudging the same objects around on my work table. I'll check the layout photos over and over again until it finally feels, I don't know, settled to me. It's frustrating because part of me knows it’s already fine, and I’m really just losing studio time by doing it, but I still feel like I have to.
Outside of these specific thoughts and routines with your artwork, do you find yourself constantly worrying about many different everyday areas of life, such as your health, finances, or family?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I guess I have normal worries about money sometimes, being an artist and all, but it's not a constant thing. It doesn't take over my day or anything. My health and family are fine. It really is just... this specific thing with my artwork that's been bothering me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits characteristic symptoms of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (ICD-10: F42), including intrusive, ego-dystonic obsessional thoughts (fear of dishonoring her aunt or not loving her enough through artistic choices) and repetitive compulsive rituals (rereading labels, repeatedly nudging objects, repeatedly checking layout photos) performed to relieve distress until feeling settled.
